concepts.name: ITC's Institutional Origin and Dual Parentage
key_dimensions: Founded in 1964 under GATT; later became joint agency of WTO and UN through UNCTAD
UPSC trap: ITC is NOT a UN agency alone — it is jointly supervised by WTO and UNCTAD (UN General Assembly)
Distinction from UNCTAD: UNCTAD is a UN body focused on policy; ITC is operational/technical assistance body
Funding structure: regular budget shared equally by WTO and UN; extra-budgetary funds from donor countries

concepts.name: ITC's Mandate and Core Mission
key_dimensions: Mandate: support sustainable development and inclusive growth through trade in developing and transition economies
Focuses on SME competitiveness — distinct from WTO (rule-making) and World Bank (finance)
Three strategic objectives: strengthen international competitiveness of enterprises, develop trade-support institutions, support policy integration
UPSC trap: ITC does NOT make trade rules or provide loans — it is purely a technical assistance and capacity-building body

concepts.name: ITC vs. UNCTAD vs. WTO — Functional Overlap and Differentiation
key_dimensions: WTO: rule-setting and dispute resolution; UNCTAD: research, policy advocacy, intergovernmental consensus; ITC: operational trade development
ITC works at the enterprise/business level; UNCTAD and WTO work at the government/policy level
ITC is the only multilateral agency exclusively focused on SME internationalisation
UPSC trap: All three may appear in options — differentiating their operational domains is critical

concepts.name: ITC Headquarters and Governance Structure
key_dimensions: Headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland — same city as WTO
Governed by the Joint Advisory Group (JAG): oversees ITC's work programme and budget
JAG composition: members of both WTO and UNCTAD Trade and Development Board
Executive Director leads ITC; reports to both WTO Director-General and UNCTAD Secretary-General

concepts.name: ITC's Key Flagship Programmes — SheTrades Initiative
key_dimensions: SheTrades: global initiative to connect 3 million women entrepreneurs to market by 2021
Addresses gender gap in international trade — women-owned businesses face disproportionate barriers
UPSC angle: SheTrades is often cited in context of SDG 5 (Gender Equality) and SDG 8 (Decent Work)
SheTrades Commonwealth: specific programme under Commonwealth framework — distinct from core SheTrades

concepts.name: ITC's Trade Map and Market Analysis Tools
key_dimensions: Trade Map: free online tool providing trade statistics for 220 countries and 5,300 products
Helps exporters, policymakers, and researchers identify markets and suppliers
Other tools: Market Access Map (tariff data), Investment Map, Standards Map, Procurement Map
UPSC relevance: these tools support evidence-based trade policy — often cited in export promotion discussions

concepts.name: ITC and the Aid for Trade (AfT) Framework
key_dimensions: ITC is a key implementing partner of WTO's Aid for Trade initiative launched at Hong Kong Ministerial (2005)
Aid for Trade helps developing countries build trade infrastructure and supply-side capacity
ITC receives significant extra-budgetary resources through AfT mechanisms
UPSC trap: Aid for Trade is a WTO initiative; ITC implements it — do not conflate the two

concepts.name: ITC's Focus on Least Developed Countries (LDCs)
key_dimensions: ITC dedicates over 50% of its technical assistance to LDCs and sub-Saharan Africa
Supports LDC graduation by building export diversification and value-chain integration
Programmes: Enhanced Integrated Framework (EIF) — ITC is a co-supervisor alongside UNCTAD, WTO, World Bank, IMF, UNDP
UPSC trap: EIF is a multi-donor programme specifically for LDCs — ITC is one of six core agencies, not the sole implementer

concepts.name: Enhanced Integrated Framework (EIF) — ITC's Role
key_dimensions: EIF: multi-donor programme to mainstream trade into national development plans of LDCs
Six core agencies: ITC, UNCTAD, WTO, World Bank, IMF, UNDP — each with specific roles
ITC's role: technical assistance for export competitiveness and private sector development
UPSC angle: EIF is linked to SDG 17 (Partnerships for Goals) and LDC graduation agenda

concepts.name: ITC's NTM (Non-Tariff Measures) Business Surveys
key_dimensions: ITC conducts NTM surveys in 50+ countries to identify trade barriers faced by businesses
NTMs include SPS measures, TBT, customs procedures — often more restrictive than tariffs in modern trade
ITC's NTM data feeds into WTO negotiations and national trade facilitation strategies
UPSC relevance: NTMs are central to Trade Facilitation Agreement (TFA) discussions and India's export challenges

concepts.name: ITC and the WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement (TFA)
key_dimensions: TFA (2017): first multilateral agreement since WTO's formation; aims to cut customs red tape
ITC provides technical assistance to developing countries for TFA implementation (Category C measures)
ITC's tools like NTM surveys and Supply Chain Management programmes directly support TFA goals
UPSC trap: TFA was concluded at Bali Ministerial (2013), entered into force 2017 — ITC implements, does not negotiate

concepts.name: ITC's Standards Map and Global Value Chain Integration
key_dimensions: Standards Map: comprehensive database of voluntary sustainability standards (VSS) across sectors
Helps exporters from developing countries comply with private standards (e.g., Fair Trade, Rainforest Alliance)
Critical for agri-food and textile sectors — key export sectors for India and other developing countries
UPSC angle: VSS can act as de facto non-tariff barriers — ITC helps bridge the compliance gap

concepts.name: ITC's World Export Development Forum (WEDF)
key_dimensions: WEDF: ITC's flagship annual conference bringing together exporters, policymakers, and trade support institutions
Focuses on specific themes: digital trade, SME finance, women in trade, sustainable supply chains
Provides a platform for South-South cooperation and knowledge exchange
UPSC relevance: WEDF outputs often feed into G20, WTO, and UNCTAD discussions on trade and development

concepts.name: ITC and India — Bilateral Engagement
key_dimensions: India is both a beneficiary and a donor country to ITC's technical assistance programmes
ITC has partnered with APEDA, FIEO, and other Indian trade bodies for export capacity building
SheTrades India: dedicated programme to integrate Indian women entrepreneurs into global value chains
ITC supports India's 'Make in India' and export diversification goals — relevant to GS-3 trade policy

concepts.name: ITC's Role in Sustainable and Green Trade
key_dimensions: ITC's Sustainability Map integrates environmental and social standards into trade promotion
Supports developing countries in meeting EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) requirements
Green trade programmes align with SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption) and SDG 13 (Climate Action)
UPSC trap: CBAM is an EU mechanism; ITC helps developing countries adapt to it — do not conflate the two

concepts.name: ITC's SME Competitiveness Framework
key_dimensions: ITC's SME Competitiveness Grid: diagnostic tool assessing firm-level, immediate business environment, and national environment
Three capacity levels: COMPETE (firm), CONNECT (linkages), CHANGE (policy environment)
SME focus distinguishes ITC from other multilateral bodies that focus on macro-level trade
UPSC angle: SME internationalisation is central to inclusive growth narrative in developing economies

concepts.name: ITC's Alliances for Action — Multi-Stakeholder Coalitions
key_dimensions: ITC convenes multi-stakeholder coalitions of businesses, governments, and civil society for specific trade challenges
Examples: Alliance for Action on Sustainable Cocoa, Coffee, and Textile supply chains
Distinct from intergovernmental negotiations — private sector-led with ITC as convener
UPSC relevance: linked to commodity-dependent developing economies and price volatility challenges

concepts.name: ITC's Budget, Funding Model, and Accountability
key_dimensions: Regular budget: ~50% from WTO, ~50% from UN (through UNCTAD) — approximately CHF 47 million annually
Extra-budgetary resources (donor-funded projects): 3–4 times larger than regular budget
Major donors: EU, UK, Switzerland, Netherlands, Nordic countries — NOT the USA as a dominant funder
UPSC trap: ITC's financial dependence on extra-budgetary donors raises questions about mandate neutrality

concepts.name: ITC and Digital Trade / E-Commerce for SMEs
key_dimensions: ITC's eTrade for All initiative: multi-agency effort to help developing countries leverage e-commerce
ITC specifically focuses on connecting SMEs to cross-border e-commerce platforms (B2B and B2C)
Supports WTO's Joint Statement Initiative (JSI) on e-commerce — builds developing country capacity to participate
UPSC angle: digital trade governance is a frontier issue at WTO; ITC's role is capacity-building, not rule-making

concepts.name: ITC's Relationship with Regional Bodies and South-South Cooperation
key_dimensions: ITC works with ASEAN, AU, COMESA, and other regional bodies to scale trade facilitation
South-South cooperation: ITC facilitates knowledge transfer between middle-income and LDC countries
India-Africa trade corridor: ITC has supported capacity building aligning with India's development cooperation
UPSC angle: ITC's regional programmes often appear in context of India's neighbourhood and Africa policy
